dedupe_keys.name: citylines collaborative open data on transit systems and their historical evolution

description: Citylines is a collaborative platform for mapping the transit systems of the world, with an emphasis on the historical evolution of networks. The project README says the data stored on the platform is open and can be downloaded in different formats and scales from the data page, and that anyone can improve or add data through the online editor. The platform code is MIT licensed. Coverage: cities worldwide as mapped by contributors, including lines and stations over time. Format and access: downloads without registration. Licence and cost: free and described as open; the exact data licence is not stated in the pages read. Caveats: crowdsourced, so completeness and accuracy vary by city, and the data page is rendered by script. It supports network flow studies and analyses of how networks grew, such as testing a model on past network states. It relates to OpenStreetMap, BRTData and the GTFS specification in the catalogue.
